extracted.intended_audience: Applicants, reference writers, and panelists for the NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP)
extracted.subtask_description: Official Frequently Asked Questions describing eligibility, merit review criteria, formatting, transcript and reference letter rules, deadlines, and panelist requirements for applicants to the NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (GRFP).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program eligibility (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: Eligibility requirements for the GRFP competition are contained in Section IV of the Program Solicitation (NSF 16-588).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are strongly encouraged to read the Program Solicitation for full rules and to contact the GRF Operations Center with questions. This FAQ provides clarifications but refers to the Solicitation for official guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / residency requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must be U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals, or permanent residents at the time of application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign nationals in the U.S. on a student visa are ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Previous GRFP award recipients ineligible
rubrics_metrics.description: If you have received and accepted a GRFP award, you cannot apply for a second GRFP award.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also, failure to notify NSF of acceptance/decline by the published deadline makes you ineligible to apply again.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligibility for joint science-professional degrees
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants planning to pursue a joint science-professional degree (e.g., MD/Ph.D., JD/Ph.D.) are ineligible for GRFP even if proposing to use the fellowship only for the Ph.D. portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants who are enrolled or plan to enroll in a graduate degree program while on leave from a professional degree or joint program are also ineligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate-student one-time application rule and 12-month limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate students may apply only once while enrolled in graduate school, and only if they have completed no more than 12 months of graduate study by the application deadline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a one-time-in-graduate-school rule (updated in 2016). Applicants should be strategic about timing and consult advisors. Applications submitted before beginning graduate study do not count toward this one-time graduate-school limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Counting graduate study toward the limit (full-time vs part-time, credit-hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: GRFP allows no more than 12 months full-time graduate study or its equivalent; for part-time students the equivalent is 24 semester hours or 36 quarter hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The limit applies to all post-baccalaureate graduate study (across programs/fields). Full-time students are judged by time in program, not by an overload of credits taken within 12 months.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-degree and post-baccalaureate graduate coursework counts
rubrics_metrics.description: All post-baccalaureate graduate-level study completed outside a degree program counts toward the graduate-study limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you have both part-time non-degree coursework and full-time graduate study, total part-time credits should not exceed 24 semester / 36 quarter hours as of Aug 1 of application year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graduate coursework taken as an undergraduate does not count
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate-level courses taken while still an undergraduate (before earning a bachelor's degree) do not count toward the 12-month graduate-study limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Joint baccalaureate-master's programs have separate rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception: coursework required to maintain professional credentials
rubrics_metrics.description: Graduate coursework required to establish or maintain professional credentials (e.g., teaching credentials) is not counted toward the 12-month limit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception applies only to coursework required to maintain credentials for a job, not coursework to prepare for a future job.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interruption exception to prior graduate study limit
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants who completed more than 12 months of graduate study may be eligible if they had an interruption in graduate study of at least two consecutive years immediately prior to November 1 of the application year and have completed no additional graduate study by August 1 of the application year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You cannot be already enrolled in graduate school at the time you apply after such an interruption. You must address reasons for the interruption in the Personal, Relevant Background and Future Goals Statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Joint BS/MS program handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Individuals in joint BS/MS or BA/MA programs are eligible to apply in the final year of the program or after completion, provided they have not completed additional graduate credits after earning the joint degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A joint degree is defined as enrollment simultaneously as an undergraduate and master's student and must be reflected in the transcript. Successive enrollment in bachelor's then master's does not count as joint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field-of-study eligibility (clinical, biomedical, engineering)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain clinical practice-focused and patient-oriented research fields are ineligible (examples: clinical practice counseling, social work, patient-oriented research, epidemiological/medical behavioral studies, outcomes research, health services research). Some biomedical research is ineligible (e.g., biology programs doing biomedical research). Engineering-focused biomedical work may be eligible if primarily advancing engineering knowledge (select biomedical engineering as primary field).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Section IV.3 of the Program Solicitation for official lists and guidance; eligibility depends on whether the proposed study advances the scholarly field rather than clinical practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Merit review criteria — Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: The Merit Review Criteria for GRFP are Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate both criteria holistically across the entire application. Evidence considered for Intellectual Merit includes the Personal, Relevant Background and Future Goals Statement, Graduate Research Plan, academic record, prior research experience/publications/presentations, and references. Broader Impacts consider potential to benefit society and contribute to desired societal outcomes through research and non-research activities, including broadening participation in STEM.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holistic review guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: Holistic review assesses applicants' interests and competencies in a flexible, individualized way, balancing experiences, attributes, and academic achievements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should present a coherent combination of experiences and achievements that demonstrate potential for significant research achievements in STEM and STEM education.

rubrics_metrics.name: No prescribed weighting between criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no specific limit on how much weight to give each criterion in your statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should demonstrate both Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts thoroughly in both statements so reviewers can access and evaluate evidence easily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content boundary — only FastLane materials considered
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers are instructed to evaluate only the evidence provided within the FastLane application; links to external material or extraneous documents will not be considered and will be marked extraneous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include manuscripts, resumes, medical reports, news clippings, videos, or links except as part of References Cited. All materials must be uploaded to FastLane by the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement formatting requirements (font, margins, spacing)
rubrics_metrics.description: Statements must use 8.5" x 11" page size, 12-point Times New Roman or Computer Modern (LaTeX) font, 1" margins on all sides, and be single spaced or greater. References, footnotes, and figure captions may be 10-point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to follow any of these guidelines will result in an application being returned without review. Character spacing should be normal and single-line spacing or greater must be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement page limits and inclusions
rubrics_metrics.description: Personal, Relevant Background and Future Goals Statement: 3-page limit. Graduate Research Plan Statement: 2-page limit. All references, footnotes, citations, images, etc., must be included within these page limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Graduate Research Plan exceeds two pages (e.g., references on a third page) the application will be returned without review. An extra completely blank trailing page will not cause return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identifying information on statements
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not required to put your name, applicant ID, or other identifying information on the statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Including name or similar identifying information in the 1" margins is allowed as long as the identifying information does not contain meaningful statement content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on "exactly 12 point" line spacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should not use an "exactly 12 point" line spacing setting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the standard single-spaced setting; exactly 12-point removes the small vertical cushion and results in a more condensed page that is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: LaTeX-specific guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: LaTeX users may use Computer Modern or Times New Roman; specify 12-point font because LaTeX defaults to 10-point. Statements prepared in LaTeX must follow the same formatting requirements as those prepared with word processors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References and figure captions may be 10-point; ensure the final PDF, when previewed in FastLane, complies with layout rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: FastLane upload preview and formatting compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should preview uploaded statements in FastLane. Application status is based on the contents submitted in FastLane; if the uploaded version does not comply with formatting requirements, it may be returned without review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload and preview well in advance of deadlines to resolve PDF/upload issues. An extra blank page that is completely blank will not cause return.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcripts — acceptability and redaction
rubrics_metrics.description: You may upload either official or unofficial transcripts as long as unofficial transcripts meet GRFP Solicitation requirements. Applicants are encouraged to redact sensitive personally identifiable information (date of birth, SSN) before uploading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your school doesn't provide electronic transcripts you may upload a scanned hard-copy transcript; if you just started and have no transcript, upload an unofficial transcript, course schedule, or enrollment verification showing courses registered for.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcripts — password-protected or encrypted files not accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: FastLane does not accept password-protected or similarly encrypted PDF transcripts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your school's electronic transcripts are encrypted, obtain an unencrypted unofficial copy or scan a hard copy. If you receive an upload error, print the transcript and scan to PDF before uploading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutions and transcript upload requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: List all institutions from which you received a bachelor's degree or higher and upload transcripts from all institutions listed. You must include transcripts from all graduate study done after you obtained your first baccalaureate degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For multiple baccalaureate institutions attended prior to the first degree, inclusion is discretionary, but all graduate study after the first baccalaureate must be listed and transcribed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters — submission channel and counts
rubrics_metrics.description: All reference letters must be submitted online through FastLane. You will list reference writers and assign priority rankings; if more than three letters are submitted, only the three you listed as highest priority will be included in the application package for review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference writers must receive the nomination email; applicants must hit 'Send Email' when adding writers. You may change priority rankings up until the application due date, even if a letter has already been submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference letters — formatting and page limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters of reference are limited to a maximum of 2 pages; FastLane will not accept letters longer than 2 pages. Letters should use standard 8.5" x 11" page size, 12-point Times New Roman or Computer Modern font, 1" margins, single spaced or greater, normal (100%) character spacing, and should be signed and on professional letterhead if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FastLane enforces the two-page limit; ensure letters adhere to formatting. If only two reference letters are received, the application may still be reviewed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference-letter technical troubleshooting guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If a reference writer does not receive nomination or temporary password emails, check that the applicant hit 'Send Email,' verify the accuracy of the reference writer's email address, and check spam folders. If necessary, use an alternate email address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reference letter requests are associated with email addresses — if the same writer is listed under different emails by different applicants, the writer may need to create a separate login or the applicant must edit the email to match. Contact info@nsfgrfp.org for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application deadlines and timezone rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be submitted by the deadline time; NSF must receive your application by 5 p.m. local time as determined by the applicant's mailing address on the Field of Study specific deadline day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There are no exceptions for late submissions. Reference letters deadline: first Thursday in November, 5 p.m. Eastern Time; track reference submission status in FastLane.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, reviews availability, and appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewed applicants will be notified by early April via email to the FastLane-registered address. Reviews are available for download in FastLane for a limited time and are the only available feedback; per NSF policy there is no reconsideration or appeal of fellowship award decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you did not receive notification check spam/trash and then contact info@nsfgrfp.org with name, 10-digit applicant ID, and primary mailing address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application content from past successful applications not available
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of past successful applications or statements from previously awarded applicants are not available from NSF's GRFP.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should not expect to obtain or rely on prior applicants' statements from NSF.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interdisciplinary field selection and panel assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: If selecting multiple fields due to interdisciplinary work, your application will be assigned to review according to the primary field you select; reviewers are drawn from that panel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose the primary field that best matches your research interests and consult advisors. Check prospective panels and component fields on the GRFP website.

rubrics_metrics.name: GRE scores not required
rubrics_metrics.description: GRE scores are not part of the GRFP application and are not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include GRE scores in application materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supplemental materials and links prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants cannot include links or supplemental material (papers, videos, etc.) for reviewers to consider; only materials uploaded to FastLane are reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any material outside FastLane will be marked extraneous and not considered; only citations in References Cited may include web links as part of references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application re-application and withdrawn/returned without review handling
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications submitted prior to graduate enrollment do not count toward the graduate-student one-time limit. Applications that are withdrawn before review or returned without review do not count toward the one-application limit for graduate students.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you are offered an award but decline before the acceptance deadline you may be ineligible to reapply depending on circumstances; consult the Solicitation and GRF Operations Center.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panelist duties, orientation, and review load
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective panelists register interest; invitations are issued after needs assessment. Accepted panelists must participate in an orientation webinar and review up to 30 or fewer applications in December.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Panelists must view the orientation webinar even if previously served; panel meetings held online via WebEx and panelists should prepare technologically in advance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panelist flat rate fee and eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Panelists receive a Flat Rate Fee for participation in virtual panel sessions (minimum 4-hour duration). Panelists must participate at least four hours in a session to receive the fee; U.S. citizenship is required and federal government employees are not eligible for the fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Payment is via Electronic Funds Transfer using NSF Guest Travel and Reimbursement System; email with registration instructions will be sent in December.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel logistics and required technology
rubrics_metrics.description: All GRFP panel meetings take place online using WebEx; panelists need a computer with internet access, a land-line phone, and are advised to use a wired internet connection rather than wireless.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed instructions for WebEx testing and access will be sent to panelists prior to meetings.
